title: Forces and Magnets
seo_title: Grade 2 Science: Forces and Magnets Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Forces influence the motion of an object: contact forces and at-a-distance forces (magnets, static electricity), balanced and unbalanced forces, and how objects move over different materials. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 2, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 science worksheets (BC): pushes and pulls, friction, gravity, magnets that attract and repel, and magnetic materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Magnets and gravity can pull without touching.
body_html:
How to think about it

Forces change how things move.

  • Friction slows things down.
  • Gravity pulls things down.
  • Magnets attract iron and steel.
Example

Which surface has more friction: ice or carpet?

Things slide easily on ice.

Answer: carpet

Example

Will a magnet pick up a paper clip?

Paper clips are steel.

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking magnets attract all metals (aluminum and copper are not attracted).
  • Thinking gravity only works on heavy things.

items.q: Is this a contact force or a non-contact force: friction between shoes and the floor?
c: a non-contact force (it acts at a distance)
items.e: Most forces need things to touch. Magnetism and gravity act at a distance.

items.q: The two magnets are pushed towards each other. What happens?
items.e: Unlike poles attract; like poles repel.

items.q: What happens when a north pole and a south pole are near each other?
items.e: Unlike poles attract.

items.q: Explain what happens when these magnets are brought together.
c: A north pole faces a south pole, and unlike poles attract.
Two north poles face each other, and like poles repel.
Magnets only work when they touch.
items.e: Look at the two ends that face each other.

items.q: Three magnets are pushed together in this order. What happens between the left magnet and the middle magnet?
items.e: Look at the two ends that face each other: like poles repel, unlike poles attract.

items.q: Which two poles are facing each other?
c: the south pole of the left magnet and the south pole of the right magnet
the south pole of the left magnet and the north pole of the right magnet
the north pole of the left magnet and the south pole of the right magnet
the north pole of the left magnet and the north pole of the right magnet
items.e: Look at the letters on the two inside ends.
